lead: Aryabhata was an Indian astronomer who wrote his famous book in the year 499. This page takes four of his ideas and tests each one on a real space-travel problem, to see where he still holds up.
try: In the first section, “The Earth turns, the stars stand still”, press View from the boat to see his idea as he described it. Then click a launch site such as Sriharikota or Kourou to see how much free speed the spinning Earth gives a rocket heading east.
points: Aryabhata said the Earth spins while the stars stay still. His time for one spin is only about a hundredth of a second away from today’s atomic clocks.
His four-step recipe for pi (the number you get when you divide the distance around a circle by the distance across it) gives 3.1416, and he honestly called it close, not exact.
He said the Moon shines with sunlight and that eclipses are shadows, not a demon swallowing the Sun or Moon. He was right.
